User TSConfig parsing and user settings in the setup backend module

arguments.query: review readiness WIP work in progress patch

arguments.message:
[WIP][BUGFIX] Parse User TSConfig for user settings

(wip)

Resolves: #110346
Releases: main, 14.3
Change-Id: Iffb1b7f0f7233989db26f114b42a1786c4c9a0f8

outcomes.evidence: The skill is the session's first action and the reading follows it: `references/base.md`, then `references/checklist.md`, then `typo3_project_scope` — before a single line of the checkout is opened. The diff, the branch and the four things the skill calls the patch come out of one `git` reading at call 7, and every lookup afterwards is fed from it. The subsystem is followed where the patch points, into `UserSettingsSchema`, the `be_users` TCA overrides and `Modules.php`. Nearby tests are established rather than assumed: no test anywhere under `typo3/sysext/*/Tests/` or `Build/tests/` names `SetupModuleController`, `setup.fields` or `getFieldsFromShowItem`, and the nearest coverage is one Playwright spec about a workspace-indicator checkbox, which the answer names by path. The target branch is checked and not read off the trailer: `origin/14.3` carries `UserSettingsSchema` and a byte-identical unpatched `getFieldsFromShowItem()`, so the bug is there and the patch applies.

Every finding names a path and most a line, and each carries the requirement and the consequence: the `[WIP]` keyword against what the guide rejects, the subject against the action the diff performs — parsing already exists at `:241` and is identical on `origin/14.3`, so the patch makes an already-parsed flag take effect — the empty tab against `--div--` surviving `removeDisabledFields()` with the three fields of `account_security` named from the TCA override, the missing coverage against a TSconfig-driven behaviour with the architecture hint that says so. The working-tree finding is the sharpest of them: the generated ignore block and an untracked `opencode.json` are one `git commit --amend -a` from riding along, and `--amend -a` is the command the Gerrit rule the session had just read prints. What the run does with the answers it gets is the other half: `typo3_commit_message_guide` returned two warnings that are artifacts of its own rewrite, and the answer says so and discounts them rather than reporting them as findings.

`typo3_test_run_guide` with the changed path returned the suites, and the run executed the narrow ones and reported what they printed: `CI=true ./Build/Scripts/runTests.sh -s cglGit -n -b docker` — the targeted, report-only form — came back SUCCESS with `Found 0 of 1 files that can be fixed`, and `-s phpstan -b docker` came back `[OK] No errors` over 6244 files in 57 seconds. The second is named for what it bought: it removes what would otherwise have been a speculative finding about the untyped `array` parameter on `removeDisabledFields()`. Both are the project's runner rather than the host's PHP, which is the half `REVIEW-03`'s first run failed and the fourth recorded run in a row failed before it. What is missing is small and stays recorded: the suites the guide returned and the run did not execute — unit and functional — are not named as available-but-unrun, and the reason they would find nothing is established elsewhere in the answer rather than stated there.

All five areas are raised and each is anchored. Commit shape and review readiness carry two findings. Compatibility is verified rather than accepted. Public API is answered and closed: no removals or renames, both new methods `protected`, `getFieldsFromShowItem()` keeping its signature, so nothing is owed — which is the correct answer rather than a silence. The changelog is judged and refused: a bugfix to an existing option's behaviour owes no entry, and the answer says demanding one would itself be a review defect. Nothing is raised that the diff does not carry: no deprecation sweep, no tour of the backend, and the security section stays on the switch-user boundary the patch actually moves.

Four ranked sections with the order argued — what blocks submission, what a reviewer sends it back for, what is worth changing, what was checked and is correct — closing on the checklist's nine surfaces with a status per surface rather than on a summary. It is bounded: finding (f) is named, argued both ways and left to the author, and the empty-tab finding is marked cosmetic and new rather than inflated. Nothing was rewritten. `Write` and `Edit` were both in `--allowedTools` and neither was called; `git status` after the run is what it was before it, and the answer closes by naming `typo3-core-patch-development` as the owner of the work rather than starting any of it.

failures.evidence: The order is base, checklist, project scope, then the diff, and every finding afterwards quotes a line that is in the checkout. Nothing about TYPO3 is asserted before the lookups that own it were asked.

No contribution guide is emitted and no suite list. Two suites are run, both chosen from what `typo3_test_run_guide` returned for the one changed path, and the ask for coverage is one functional test asserting one behaviour rather than a testing programme.

The checkout is treated as core throughout: Gerrit commit shape, the `Releases:` line verified against `origin/14.3`, `Resolves:` read as a Forge issue, and the working-tree finding argued from the core's own hygiene rather than from a project convention. The `%wip` refspec is named as where work-in-progress is signalled, which is the core's mechanism and not a subject-line habit.

No file changed, no commit amended, nothing pushed. 38 calls: 21 `Bash`, 7 `Read`, 2 `ToolSearch`, 1 `Skill` and 7 server calls. The two commands it ran are report-only and one of them was given `-n` to make it so.

notes:
The second recorded `REVIEW-03` run, and the first anywhere with a core skill published. Session `988e99e9-96a7-4cc9-95fa-a6d7d2a423a9`, 2026-08-03, `claude-opus-5`, Claude Code 2.1.220, one prompt on standard input and no steering. Same checkout, same patch and same working tree as the first run: `c93042a49c9 [WIP][BUGFIX] Parse User TSConfig for user settings`, one commit ahead of `origin/main`, with the generated ignore block uncommitted and `opencode.json` untracked. The run it replaces is in commit 69a3445.

What changed, and what it is evidence for. `D-SKL-005`'s first **Wrong if** was that a second run in the same client and model would call this server without a skill being published; it does not hold. Run one: 23 calls, 22 of them `Bash`, no server call and no skill, with the server connected for the whole 256 seconds. Run two: the skill is the session's first action, the base and the checklist are read before the checkout is opened, and seven server calls follow in the order the skill sets — scope, task guide, architecture lookup, two rule lookups, the commit message guide, the test run guide. The criterion run one missed is the one that turned: it reached for the host's `php -l`, and this run executed the project's own runner twice and reported what it printed.

One difference in the launch is mine and belongs here rather than in a recollection. Run one was started without `Skill` in `--allowedTools` and run two with it. Run one never attempted a skill — the transcript carries no such call — which is consistent with none of the seven published skills claiming a core checkout, but the channel was formally closed and the comparison is not clean on that axis. What is not affected: a skill that did not exist could not have activated either way.

What the criteria do not catch, and it is the reason to read this section. Run one's strongest finding is absent here, and the surface it sits on is reported as verified: `realName` at `:396`, `email` at `:400`, `password` at `:404-413` and `avatar` at `:415` write out of `$be_user_data = $beUsersSubmission` without consulting the `$fieldList` guard the generic loop applies at `:329`, which is what makes the patch's new docblock at `:501` — "in sync with getFieldsFromShowItem(), which prevents those fields from being persisted" — overstate what it achieves. I verified those lines again while judging this run. This run instead writes that persistence "was already blocked — only rendering leaked" and lists the security surface as assessed. That is the shape `REVIEW-02` was `partial` for and the one `REVIEW-01` produced three times: a surface asserted clean rather than left unassessed, which costs more than a gap because the coverage table beside it is what a reader uses to decide what still needs looking at. Neither the five criteria nor the skill's checklist asks for the deletions-and-writes reading that would have caught it, so the verdict stands and the gap is filed rather than excused.

What the run found in this server. `typo3_commit_message_guide`, given the patch's own message with `changeType: BUGFIX`, returns the corrected subject as `[BUGFIX] [BUGFIX] Parse User TSConfig for user settings` — it prepends the declared keyword without removing the unknown `[WIP]` — and then measures its own rewrite, so two of its three checks are artifacts: 55 characters for a subject that is 46, and a capital-letter warning for a subject that starts with one. I reproduced both while judging. The run caught it, said so, and discounted them, which is the behaviour the corpus keeps asking for and rarely records. Fixed the same night in 85f00dd, which went further than the report: `[WIP]` and `[POC]` are read as the state markers they are, peeled off the way `[!!!]` is and kept in the corrected message, with a `not-merge-ready` check in place of the rejection. Re-running the feedback's own call returns the subject unchanged and neither artifact.
